title: Condorcet's paradox: majorities in a circle
intro: Three groups of voters rank the candidates A, B and C. Group 1 ranks A > B > C, group 2 ranks B > C > A and group 3 ranks C > A > B. Set the size of each group. Compare the candidates two at a time: a positive margin means a majority prefers the first candidate. When every candidate loses to another one, the majorities form a cycle and there is no Condorcet winner, yet plurality, instant runoff and the Borda count still name a winner. In the graph, an arrow points from the winner of each pair to the loser, and arrows that are part of a cycle are marked. Winners are numbered 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C; 0 means a tie or no winner.
graphTitle: Majority graph: an arrow from the winner of each pair to the loser
